NCC

  • Annual Training Camps (also called Combined Annual Training Camps) are run by NCC units under their state directorates. They are residential camps of about ten days, with training in drill, leadership, service training and social service.

    Cadets live together, follow a daily routine and build fitness, discipline and teamwork.

    General information about this type of NCC camp.

  • The Independence Day Camp is an annual NCC camp in Delhi, held around Independence Day. Cadets from across India come together, often wearing the traditional dress of their home states.

    The camp includes cultural programmes, competitions and activities that celebrate the country’s diversity.

    General information about this type of NCC camp.

  • Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (One India, Great India) is an NCC national integration camp. Cadets from paired states and union territories stay together for around ten to twelve days and learn about each other’s language, food, music and traditions.

    The camp also has guest lectures, competitions and cultural evenings, and aims to promote unity in diversity.

    General information about this type of NCC camp.

About

I’m Aman Pandey, a second-year B.Tech student in Computer Science and Engineering with a specialisation in Data Science at GTB4CEC, affiliated with Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University (IPU).

I’m building a strong foundation in programming, data analysis and problem solving, and I’m keen to apply these skills to real-world problems.

Alongside my studies, I serve as an NCC cadet. I have completed three camps so far: ATC, IDC and EBSB. They have strengthened my discipline, teamwork and leadership, and I bring the same commitment to my technical work.
